svg.title: Feature Engineering and Variable Transformation — Learning Infographic
svg.desc: One-page learning infographic with transformations, encoding, scaling, worked examples, comparisons, self-test, answers, and review schedule.
svg.text: Takeaway: choose the transformation by feature type, distribution, and model needs — not by habit.
READ LEFT → RIGHT • ARROW = PREPARATION FLOW
feature = input • target = outcome • skewness = asymmetry • residual = observed − predicted • IQR = Q3 − Q1 • transformer = learns a change, then applies it
Feature transformation changes representation; feature selection chooses which features to include. [S1, S5]
Feature engineering = modify or create useful inputs before training. [S1]
Movie example: cast budget + marketing budget → revenue. [S1]
log1p can handle zero; log can reduce positive skew;
and help model diminishing returns (effect may flatten).
Box–Cox: flexible skew transform; import not specified.
x² adds curvature; higher degrees allow more complex curves.
The model can stay linear in its coefficients even when
inputs include log(x), x², or other transformed features.
No transformation guarantees normal residuals or better performance. [S1–S2, S5]
Categories → numbers: choose by number of states and order. [S3]
WARNING: 1, 2, 3 implies equal numeric spacing — not always justified.
One-hot is also possible, but it does not express order directly. [S3]
Avoid red = 1, blue = 2, green = 3: that invents an order. [S3]
KNN uses distance: price 0–10 vs store count 10,000–50,000;
the larger-scale feature may dominate the result. [S4]
Subtract mean μ; divide by standard deviation σ.
Outliers can pull μ and inflate σ.
An extreme value can compress ordinary values.
Uses median + IQR = Q3 − Q1; less sensitive to extremes.
Does NOT guarantee values between 0 and 1.
Choose by data + purpose; no single scaler fits every case.
X_poly = polyFeat.transform(X_data) → includes degree-2 features such as x²
Fitting prepares the transformer; transform() applies it. [S5]
Transforming ≠ feature selection. Transforms do not guarantee normal residuals or good performance.
Full regression assumptions and feature-selection criteria are not covered in the source. [S1, S5]

10. Why fit a transformer before transform()?

9 It may imply equally spaced categories.

Color key: blue = concept • green = process • orange = caution • purple = memory / review
